tob-0005: Attributed to the ancient Chinese sage Laozi, this short book of eighty-one brief poems offers a philosophy of living simply and in harmony with the Tao, the way of nature. It teaches that softness overcomes hardness and that doing less often achieves more. This version is James Legge’s translation, one of the earliest English renderings. It has shaped thought in China for over two thousand years.
tob-10805: J. A. MacCulloch’s scholarly study reconstructs the religion of the ancient Celts from Roman reports, medieval Irish and Welsh tales, and the evidence of shrines and altars. He examines their gods, druids, sacrifices, and beliefs about the soul after death. The book remains a solid foundation for anyone studying how the Celts worshipped.
tob-13505: Hujviri’s eleventh-century treatise is the oldest surviving Persian manual of Sufism. Working through the doctrines of the mystics — poverty, purity of heart, trust in God — it also answers the critics who called the Sufis heretics. Reynold Nicholson’s English translation made this founding text of Islamic mysticism known to the West.
tob-4005: Baldassare Castiglione’s dialogue, set at the court of Urbino, schools the perfect gentleman in how to behave — graceful at games, witty in talk, brave in war, all without seeming to try. Carried across Europe in translation, it set the tone for noble manners for two hundred years. The book remains a sparkling picture of Renaissance high society.
tob-10508-68705: Blavatsky’s first volume of Isis Unveiled holds that the science of the 1870s, for all its wins, was blind to the deeper drives moving the world. tob-10808-50205: Baron Friedrich von Hügel’s weighty study of Saint Catherine of Genoa probes the mystic strand in faith through her life and writings. tob-0143-68705: Blavatsky’s Isis Unveiled, first volume, aims at the science of the 1870s — holding that behind matter’s show stir powers no glassware had caught. tob-0105: The Emerald Tablet is wonder-lore’s ground-text — thirteen short lines on the oneness of above and below, the one stuff whence all comes. Laid to Hermes Thrice-Great, it was the gold-makers’ bible for a thousand years. Every later work of the art cites it.

tob-12905: Manly P. Hall’s Secret Teachings of All Ages — 1928 — is the great illustrated encyclopedia of the Western mystery tradition. the-thirty-years-war-volume-05: Schiller concludes his history with the war's end and the Peace of Westphalia, which redrew the map of Europe. adventures-of-huckleberry-finn-chapters-: Mark Twain's immortal novel opens as Huck Finn, stifled by the Widow Douglas, fakes his death and flees to Jackson Island. arxiv-2605-08805: Picking out the sounding object in a video — the barking dog, the ringing phone — usually demands heavyweight neural networks. Qing Zhong, Guodong Ding, Lingqiao Liu, Zaiwen Feng, Lin Yuanbo Wu, and Angela Yao propose LightAVSeg, a lightweight audio-visual segmentation model built for speed and modest hardware. The 2026 paper trims the computation so the technique can run where resources are scarce.
arxiv-2605-08705: Unbalanced optimal transport lets mass be created or destroyed as it moves — the transport-growth pair. Donlapark Ponnoprat, Noboru Isobe, and Masaaki Imaizumi derive minimax-optimal estimators for these pairs, proving no method can do fundamentally better. The 2026 paper is statistical theory with optimality guarantees.
arxiv-2605-08905: NP-hard optimization problems — routing, scheduling — resist exact solutions, and language models are now being trained to tackle them. Xiaozhe Li, Xinyu Fang, Shengyuan Ding, and colleagues present Forge, a quality-aware reinforcement learning method that teaches LLMs to optimize. The 2026 paper trains models to be better problem-solvers, not just better talkers.
arxiv-2605-09005: Robot brains — vision-language-action models — are expensive to train and easy to steal. Ming Sun, Rui Wang, Xingrui Yu, and Lihua Jing explore backdoor-based ownership verification: planting hidden triggers that prove a model is yours. The 2026 paper is model-protection research for the coming robot economy.
arxiv-2605-09105: Molecular machines — nature's motors, and the synthetic ones we dream of — live far from equilibrium, where textbook thermodynamics falters. Ying-Jen Yang and Ken A. Dill develop nonequilibrium theory for designing such machines. The 2026 paper is statistical physics for the tiniest engines.
arxiv-2605-09205: MPEX is a planned fusion-materials experiment at Oak Ridge, and digital twins — live virtual copies — will help run it. Gary Staebler, Rhea Barnett, Mark Cianciosa, and colleagues build AI digital twins for MPEX. The 2026 paper is fusion engineering with a virtual shadow.
arxiv-2605-09505: Epilepsy diagnosis drowns in evidence — EEG traces, histories, scans — scattered across messy real-world records. Yuyang Dai, Zheng Chen, Jathurshan Pradeepkumar, and colleagues build EpiGraph: generalist AI for evidence-intensive epilepsy reasoning in the wild. The 2026 paper is medical AI for the clinic as it is.
arxiv-2605-09605: Hidden quantum Markov models describe quantum processes with latent structure, and cocycle actions bring symmetry into the picture. Abdessatar Souissi connects these actions to symmetry protection and topological order. The 2026 paper sits exactly where quantum information theory meets condensed matter.
arxiv-2605-09805: Wright's equation models delayed feedback; the stochastic version needs invariant measures to exist. M. van den Bosch, O. W. van Gaans, and S. M. Verduyn Lunel prove their existence carefully. The 2026 paper is deep stochastic delay equations, rigorously grounded throughout.
arxiv-2605-09905: Random transformers can smooth sequences adaptively — even the messy physiological signals of sleep staging. Guisong Liu, Xin Gao, Martin Dresler, and colleagues rethink them as adaptive sequence smoothers. The 2026 paper is sleep science with transformers faithfully working the night shift.
arxiv-2605-10005: Move smart contracts need specifications; combining mechanical and agentic specification inference produces them reliably. Wolfgang Grieskamp, Teng Zhang, and Vineeth Kashyap develop the combination. The 2026 paper is blockchain verification with two engines working as one. Two complementary methods yield one trusted specification.
arxiv-2605-10105: 21 cm cosmology — mapping the early universe in hydrogen's faint glow — empowered by machine learning. Hayato Shimabukuro applies ML to the 21 cm signal. The 2026 paper is cosmic-dawn science with learning machines. It learns to read the universe's first light.
plos-pone-0003405: Cancer researchers traced how tumors grow their own blood supply in this 2008 paper. The immune signal M-CSF recruits scavenger cells to tumors, and the team showed it switches on VEGF production through the MAPK/ERK pathway and the Sp1 protein. That chain builds new vessels that feed the tumor, naming several choke points future drugs might block.
plos-pone-0003505: Perception researchers rethought how the brain completes illusions in this 2008 EEG study. Kanizsa figures, shapes we see from suggestive corners alone, had always been flashed whole, but the team presented them in a notch mode, building the inducers piece by piece. Tracking the P1 and N1 brain waves clarified when and how the visual system fills in the missing contours.
plos-pone-0003605: Cell biologists Szafran, Szwarc, and Marcelli built a high-throughput window into hormone signaling in this 2008 paper. Automated imaging tracked how the androgen receptor responds to steroids, growth factors, and small molecules across the cell cycle. The platform speeds the search for drugs that tune this driver of prostate disease.
plos-pone-0003705: In 2008, Heidary, Vaeze Mahdavi, and Momeni found unfair food hurting rabbit hearts. Rabbits given unequal shares, a stand-in for low social rank, showed worse cardiac health than well-fed peers. The study models in animals how poverty and food gaps wear down the human heart.
plos-pone-0003805: Chikayama, Suto, and Nishihara brought NMR to metabolism's big picture in this 2008 paper. Their systematic analysis of isotope-labeled metabolite mixtures works across plant and animal systems. The method gives a bird's-eye view of the chemistry of life in action.
plos-pone-0003905: Working in 2008, a team modeled a pregnancy disorder in a dish. Overexpressing STOX1 in choriocarcinoma cells mimicked the gene-activity changes of preeclamptic placentas. The cell model lets researchers study a dangerous pregnancy condition without risking mothers.
plos-pone-0004005: In 2008, Milne, Kelso, and Kelly modeled flu control in a small town. Their individual-based simulation compared school closure against other possible pandemic interventions. plos-pone-0004105: In 2008, a careful team put gene-control variants to the test. Suspected regulatory variants faced an expression assay comparing both gene copies. The check confirmed which DNA tweaks truly tune nearby genes. The solid approach firms up disease-gene claims really fast.
plos-pone-0004205: In 2009, Hospedales and Vijayakumar modeled the busy brain as a statistician. Multisensory oddity detection was framed as Bayesian inference here. The model merged senses well to spot the odd one out fast. The neat math mirrors how perception fuses signals.
plos-pone-0004305: In 2009, a team found one fault silencing many genes at once. Breaking a factor above RAR-alpha triggered shutdown of a broad gene-control network fast. The single hit quieted many gene targets. The cascade links chromatin to cancer and aging both.
plos-pone-0356905: Plants under attack chop their proteins in distinctive patterns. This 4D-DIA proteomics study revealed distinct proteolytic landscapes induced by mechanical stress, Agrobacterium infection, and a viral capsid precursor. The protein-cutting maps show how plants tailor their molecular response to each different threat.
plos-pone-0357805: Floods displace families — and local news articles capture the experience in raw detail. This qualitative study examined housing displacement experiences following major flooding in regional Australia through online news coverage. The articles reveal what displacement actually feels like, beyond the statistics.
plos-pone-0357405: Knowing which AI system wrote a piece of text increasingly matters — for trust, for forensics, for accountability. SiBot is a hybrid framework for fine-grained semantic attribution of AI-generated text, already deployed in production. The system traces synthetic text back to its source model with remarkable precision.
plos-pone-0356605: People who move frequently struggle to stay in HIV care — and standard clinics fail them. This paper captured participant perspectives on a person-centred care model for mobile individuals, drawn from the SEARCH Dynamic Choice Treatment trial in rural Kenya and Uganda. Their voices guide care designed for lives in motion.
plos-pone-0356205: Radiation therapy for lung cancer too often injures the very lungs it aims to save. This protocol outlines a randomized, multicenter, controlled trial of nintedanib for preventing radiation-induced lung injury in unresectable stage II–III non-small cell lung cancer. The planned trial offers genuine hope for safer treatment.
plos-pone-0357005: Pasteurella multocida type A kills layer birds and threatens poultry economies. This paper reported its isolation, antibiogram, and whole genome sequence analysis from layer birds. The genomic data give veterinarians the tools to track, treat, and ultimately control outbreaks.
plos-pone-0357205: Combining radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy with immunotherapy before cancer surgery promises much — but is it safe? This protocol outlines a systematic review and meta-analysis of safety across solid tumors. The planned synthesis will inform one of oncology’s most pressing practice questions.
plos-pone-0355505: Exact solutions to Einstein’s field equations are rare mathematical treasures. This paper derived exact non-static cylindrical solutions with imperfect fluids. The new solutions enrich general relativity’s catalog — the equations describing gravity itself at its most extreme.
plos-pone-0356505: Cheap quadruped robots need control brains that don’t cost more than the hardware. This paper proposed a unified CPG-based and multi-agent control framework for low-cost quadruped robots. The bio-inspired framework gives budget robots remarkably lifelike, stable locomotion.
plos-pone-0352705: Anxiety and depression scales must make sense to the children they assess — in their own culture and language. Hearing teens narrate their answers reveals whether the questions truly land.
plos-pone-0355405: Uveal melanoma — eye cancer — spreads silently to the liver, demanding systematic surveillance. This paper proposed an optimized approach to that surveillance. The streamlined protocol aims to catch metastases when they’re still treatable — the difference between surveillance that saves lives and surveillance that merely documents decline.
plos-pone-0356105: Ethiopian mothers die from preventable complications that warning systems could catch. This paper developed a maternal early warning system (MEWS) model for predicting and reducing severe maternal outcomes in Ethiopia. The validated warning scores give birth attendants the trigger thresholds that turn vigilance into saved lives.
plos-pone-0356005: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma — common in Southeast Asia — needs better prognostic tools. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the three-lineage cytopenia score’s prognostic value in locally advanced disease. The simple blood-count score could help oncologists predict outcomes and tailor treatment intensity.
plos-pone-0355605: Rehabilitation researchers describe arm movements inconsistently — hampering progress. This paper bridged clinical and computational assessments by standardizing kinematic reporting in modified mallet scale movements. The reporting standard lets studies speak the same biomechanical language.
plos-pone-0355305: Predicting when a phone battery dies — on open hardware — is a modeling challenge. This paper predicted smartphone battery time-to-empty on the PinePhone using a modular electro-thermal continuous-time model. The open-source modeling advances battery transparency that proprietary phones never offer.
plos-pone-0351305: Heat-not-burn tobacco products claim to be safer — but fire risk matters too. This paper evaluated fire risk from thermal exposure of different materials under ambient conditions, comparing heat-not-burn products with combustible cigarettes. The findings inform regulators weighing the full safety profile of novel nicotine devices.
plos-pone-0354905: Korean immigrant patients navigating shared decision-making with American primary care doctors face cultural and linguistic gaps. This protocol outlines a qualitative study of their experiences. The planned research aims to make the exam room a place of genuine partnership across cultural divides.
europmc-pmc2852405: A mother's rich diet may dim her eggs' power plants, this 2010 mouse study finds. The team shows diet-fueled plumpness saps egg and zygote energy and defenses. Their tests tie a mother's meals to egg health. The link warns that pre-birth care starts with diet.
europmc-pmc2858705: The SARS virus disguises its RNA with a chemical cap to dodge defenses. This 2010 paper rebuilds that cap-methylation step in the test tube. The authors pin down the viral machinery. Their rebuild exposed a chink that future coronavirus drugs could target.
europmc-pmc2865505: Gene-expression studies drown in non-genetic noise. This 2010 paper brings a Bayesian framework that accounts for complex non-genetic factors, greatly boosting power in eQTL studies. The authors' method cleans the signal. Their advance sharpened the hunt for genes that steer expression.
europmc-pmc2865805: Drugs work better when they reach the right place, and this 2009 review tours a modern carrier. The review captured a rising technology for getting drugs where they count.
europmc-pmc2868005: Finding DNA patterns that proteins grip is core to gene regulation work. This 2010 paper offers a unified framework for motif enrichment analysis, tested on ChIP data. The authors' method spots overused patterns. Their tool sharpened the hunt for gene switches.
europmc-pmc2872605: Two broken cancer genes can team up. This 2010 paper shows kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor growth through CRAF. The authors' work reveals an unexpected partnership between seeming duds. Their finding explained why some targeted drugs backfire.
europmc-pmc3016705: Brain waves reveal the mind's split-second timing. This 2009 review explains event-related potentials, the brain's electrical echoes of thought. europmc-pmc3040205: Brazil's gene pool proved more mixed than it looks. This 2011 paper finds Brazilians share a blended ancestry across regions. The authors' finding reshapes identity debates. europmc-pmc6515705: Astrocytes are the most common cells in the brain's support crew, and they are far from identical. This review catalogs their diverse shapes - from bushy star-like forms to specialized variants - and how they remodel themselves with experience and disease. Their plasticity influences synapses, brain circuits, and behavior, placing them at the center of research into epilepsy, stroke, and neurodegeneration.
europmc-pmc6555805: Solar cells made from carbon-based plastics promise cheap, flexible power - if their efficiency climbs. By designing a chlorinated light-absorbing molecule that boosts voltage, researchers pushed organic photovoltaics past 16% efficiency, a milestone for the field. The advance shows careful molecular tuning inching plastic solar toward real-world use.
europmc-pmc6584505: Cryo-electron microscopy freezes proteins mid-pose for atomic portraits - but first, software must find thousands of tiny particles in noisy images. europmc-pmc6614205: Brains change as children grow - but most studies snap single pictures instead of filming the change. Latent change score models turn repeated brain measures into true developmental trajectories. This tutorial shows developmental neuroscientists how to use them, with worked examples of what growing minds reveal.
europmc-pmc6688105: Most disease-linked DNA variants hide in the genome's dark matter - noncoding regions whose job is regulation. Using saturation mutagenesis, researchers rewrote twenty disease-associated regulatory elements letter by letter to map each base's effect. The base-resolution atlas links tiny variants to real biological consequences.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-105: GAO's 2007 report looks at why old age hits women's wallets harder. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1005: Federal development grants came with strings — and GAO's 2007 report says nobody was watching the strings. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-805: The nation's consolidated books were still shaky in 2007 — GAO's audit finds big control holes in how the federal financial statements got built. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-505: VA computers kept growing legs in 2007 — GAO's report says weak controls over tech gear at picked sites meant theft stayed easy. The findings describe locks that did not lock. The report warns that a missing laptop is a missing veteran's identity.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-705: Cyber crooks were outpacing the cops in 2007 — GAO's report says public agencies and private firms alike struggled with the hacker threat. The findings map the shared battlefield. The report's plea: the good guys need to team up, because the bad guys already have.
gao-gaoreports-b-299305: Mathews Associates took its March 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest in full. Every protest gets the same careful reading.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-205: Katrina contracting data stayed holey in 2007, and GAO's report again says the subcontracting records for small firms needed completing. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-105: The nuclear regulator's workforce was aging out in 2007, and GAO's report says retirements and new reactor applications would strain the staff. openalex-w7207646205: Every Brazilian school has a pedagogical coordinator, the person who bridges teachers, principals, and curriculum. pmc-13454505: A 2026 perspective on the future of detecting catecholamines — the adrenaline and dopamine family of signaling molecules. pmc-13499705: A 2026 English study projecting community-based health and social care demand associated with frailty in over-50s from 2025 to 2040 — routine data analyses and simulation (the title is truncated). The demand forecast guides planning. The simulation is the method.
pmc-13479605: In this 2026 biophysics paper, functional variants reconfigured the Rac2 conformational landscape. The disease mutations reshaped the protein's dynamics. The reconfiguration is the insight.
pmc-13420205: This 2026 OPM-MEG study found altered evening aperiodic activity and microstate dynamics in insomnia disorder. The insomniac brain's evening state was characterized. The alteration is the biomarker.
pmc-13373305: This 2026 biochemistry paper examined how physiological oxidants trigger amyloid formation of the cell cycle regulator p16INK4A. The tumor suppressor's amyloid turn was the surprise. The triggering is the mechanism.
pmc-13508805: A 2026 paper evaluating and comparing machine learning methods for type 2 diabetes classification and associated factors. The algorithms were head-to-head. The comparison guides model choice.
pmc-13472805: A 2026 review on post-stroke glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic dysfunction — mechanisms, imaging evidence, and translational challenges. The stroke's drainage failure was surveyed. The review is the roadmap.
pmc-13436105: A 2026 UK Biobank study of genetic ancestry and atrial fibrillation risk in individuals of Black ethnicity. The ancestry-AF link was tested. The risk data serve equity.
pmc-13630405: This 2026 battery paper presented thermo-kinetic design of magnesiothermic reduction for morphology-retaining porous Si@C anodes. The silicon anodes kept their shape. The design is the manufacturing advance.
pmc-13510105: This 2026 systematic review examined complement-targeted therapies in glioblastoma. The immune-targeting evidence was pooled. The review is the neuro-oncology outlook.
arxiv-2606-16205: The 'two-line' trick is a slick path to true answers — lone waves and such — for twisty math rules. This paper is a first tour: how to spot which rules bow to the trick and how to bend them into shape. A primer for wave-math and earth-math students.
arxiv-2606-16405: A pure math paper that nails two bedrock 'no-runaway' rules — Harnack and Poincaré checks — for rough, jagged math lands with no smooth skin. Such checks are the spine of true-math on harsh ground. For shape-measure pros. Dry, dense, and built to last.
arxiv-2606-16605: Robots and game agents increasingly plan with learned "world models" — but those models can be fooled by small perturbations. ARB4WM is a benchmark for adversarial robustness of world models in continuous control: it tests whether an agent's internal model holds up under attack. It targets RL safety researchers.
arxiv-2606-16705: When particles graze each other at nearly the speed of light, they diffract — and "diffractive structure functions" describe what emerges. This paper computes them from JIMWLK evolution, the equations governing gluons at extreme energies. It targets high-energy physicists studying the dense gluon frontier of matter.
